prompts.title: Weekly carrier report
prompts.summary: Turns your load list into a one-page weekly report for each carrier.
prompts.prompt: Here are this week's loads for [carrier]: [paste load number, lane, miles, rate, deadhead, status]. Write a one-page report: totals (loads, loaded miles, gross, rate per mile, deadhead %), my fee at [%], one line per load, anything still owed (PODs, detention), and next week's plan in two lines. Plain and short.
prompts.use: Send Friday afternoon, the same format every week.

prompts.title: Rate con check
prompts.summary: A checklist to read a rate confirmation for the things that cost a carrier later.
prompts.prompt: Read this rate confirmation and list, in plain words: pickup and delivery windows, the all-in rate and how it splits, detention and layover terms, lumper terms, TONU, payment terms, any fines or penalties, and anything that looks different from what was said on the phone: [paste rate con text].
prompts.use: Run it before your carrier signs. Ask the broker about anything it flags.

prompts.title: Service agreement outline
prompts.summary: An outline of what your dispatch agreement should cover, to take to a lawyer.
prompts.prompt: Outline a dispatch service agreement between [my business] and a carrier. Cover: what I do and don't do, which loads I find for this carrier (lanes and equipment, so I never choose between carriers for one load), my fee and when it's paid, who signs rate cons, the carrier's right to refuse a load, how either side ends it, and what records I keep. Mark it as an outline for a lawyer to review, not a contract.
prompts.use: Have a lawyer turn it into your agreement before you sign carriers.

notes: FMCSA's 2023 guidance: a dispatcher who works for more than one carrier and chooses which carrier gets a load is acting as a broker and needs broker authority. Handling money between shippers and carriers points the same way. The agreement outline sets which loads you find for each carrier (lanes, equipment) so you never choose between carriers for one load. Have a lawyer check it.
